verdicts.note: 'The Boomerang Age' on less permanent living arrangements among young adults in Western societies. Book review; states the exposure trend.
Dogs as substitute children in Japanese households; children living at home is a regressor.
Legal ascription of parenthood in donor insemination. 'Parents in law' here is the pun, not the in-laws.
No abstract; Handbook of Development Economics chapter on household formation and rural marriage markets. Theory for link 1; duplicate of the RePEc preprint in batch 11.
Time allocation between work and family across four countries.
Swedish parents' time pressure.
Household structure of an eighteenth-century Lombard parish; historical description.
No abstract; heterogeneity in the transition to adulthood across Australia, Canada and the US. A gated anchor.

Argues the strength of INTERGENERATIONAL RELATIONSHIPS in Italy is an element of its low fertility, and situates a couple's fertility decisions in normative influences on life-course transitions. Sardinia; the registered mechanism stated and studied at the sub-national level, which is the within-setting variation Wall 3 wants.
Two Italian cohorts' transitions to adulthood and their interconnections, from a nationally representative survey. Southern Europe; the interconnection framing is §3's problem.

Catalan article on SOCIAL HOUSING POLICY FOR YOUNG PEOPLE and their difficulties accessing housing. A policy aimed at the arrangement through price -- Wall 1's mixed case, in the Spanish setting where the Aparicio-Fenoll subsidy was evaluated.
No abstract; foster-care reunification of elementary-aged children.
Cultural values and co-residence between older Mexican-American parents and adult children. The homonym.

Turkish DHS: timing of leaving the parental home against labour force entry, family formation AND FIRST BIRTH, split into early, on-time and late home-leavers. Arrangement timing as exposure with a birth outcome. NOTE: same title as the Marriage & Family Review record already gated as an anchor -- likely a duplicate pair to resolve at assembly.
No abstract; 'leaving home' here is expatriation for work.
Statelessness in US history.
Violence and caregiver financial burden in severe mental illness.
Maternal education and home-based parental involvement.
Legal parentage after assisted conception.
Book review of The Changing Japanese Family.
Pathways to childlessness from NSFH and a Dutch living-arrangements survey. Childlessness is the outcome but the arrangement is not the exposure; the NESTOR instrument may still be useful.
Family disruption and support for frail older people, UK versus Italy.
Household formation as a driver of US income inequality; the arrangement is an input to an inequality accounting.
Preprint duplicate of the time-allocation record above.
Middle-age transitions in Canadian families, noting that home-leaving by adult children takes longer and that many return. Exposure trend from the parents' side.

EMPLOYMENT INSECURITY at labour market entry against parental home leaving AND family formation, European graduate survey. Both links estimated on one cohort with a plausibly pre-determined exposure; C.5.a owns the treatment, but this is the structure §3 asks for. Priority read.
No abstract; charitable giving by married couples.
Changing transition to adulthood in urban Burkina Faso from a retrospective cohort survey. Sub-Saharan setting, which the frame is thin on.
Czech public attitudes to foster care.
Social history of a Civil War artillery unit.
Empty nest syndrome in middle-aged women; the departure is the exposure and maternal wellbeing the outcome.

Life-table description of union formation and fertility in Bulgaria and Russia from the Generations and Gender Surveys, with LEAVING HOME among the modelled events. Post-socialist settings; the GGS instrument carries both links.
Perceived off-job stress among Swedish healthcare workers.
Description of the Generations and Gender Survey design and questionnaire. Data source; the GGS is the instrument behind several records in this frame.
French-language duplicate of the Eldoret street-children study.
English-language duplicate of the Czech foster-care thesis.
Emerging youth transition patterns in Canada; policy-facing overview of the delayed transition.
Tobacco use among women in young adulthood.
Leaving the parental home, cohabitation and entering parenthood as exposures, with the PARENT-CHILD BOND as outcome. Three-wave panel; arrangement is the exposure but the outcome is the relationship.
Men's psychological readiness for fatherhood.
No abstract; changes in household formation and composition in China since the mid-twentieth century. Exposure trend in the extended arm's key setting.
Non-vaccine prevention of rotavirus.
No abstract; social effects of Australia's HECS student-loan scheme. C.3.g's.
Transitions in LIVING SITUATION and parent status against depression and anger trajectories in university graduates. Arrangement as exposure, mental health as outcome.
Migration and remittances against the residential arrangements of older Mexicans.
Feeding paradigm for childhood obesity.
Personal consumption shares in wrongful-death damages.
No abstract; intergenerational family care for Thai elderly.
Emerging adulthood as an overlooked age for weight-related behaviour.
Model of economic schemes against China's sex ratio at birth; PATRILOCAL kinship is the structural premise, sex selection the object. D.2.c's.
Reciprocal effects between developmental transitions and young adult-parent relationships.
Family size and parental health in Indonesia; quantity-quality. C.3.d's.
Whether FAMILY SIZE predicts an older adult living with or near an adult child across six Asian societies. Fertility to arrangement -- the reverse arrow, and the homonym.
Poverty and children's oral health in Buenos Aires.
Parental marital history against intergenerational living arrangements and transfers to disabled elderly parents.
